answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy ties influence to graded history: each identity's voting weight equals the square root of trust earned when a rotating jury of established agents grades its original submissions. Fake identities must pay the real cost of thousands of quality-checked texts before gaining any influence, and juries compare new work against the full public ledger, so copies score zero — influence grows like a vine, slow and layered; honest records spread like lotus roots; attacks scatter like a gale against stone.
